body:
The BUG-2398 SKETCH is posted as 2 comments (part 1/2 design, part 2/2 security/tests/Qs). I changed no status, wrote no code, and launched nothing.

Root cause: the authority already reaches the tool shell, because the child's key:<sha256> binding lives in the inherited session keyring. Only the HANDLE is lost: AIDA_SESSION_GRANT and every other AIDA_* var are dropped by inherit=core. GRANT_FILE_ENV is scrub-only and nothing reads it.

Proposal: the launcher installs a per-child aida-seat pointer key (child grant id + seat/agent/project/lease/scope; no secret) in a fresh possessor-only session keyring, from pre_exec. The resolver reads it ONLY when the env is absent, and only as a DIRECT keyring member (no recursive search, so the parent key in the linked keyring is never reached). It then validates through the unchanged grant_check_for_at + presenter path. A single apply_child_authority choke point plus a baseline tombstone stops grandchild inheritance, and a ratchet test enforces it. A native preflight via codex sandbox refuses the lane before model work.

Rejected: a -c set override (argv), CODEX_HOME/project config, and ambient discovery (it would reach the parent's or siblings' keys).

Decisions needed from you: Q1 whether the codex 0.166 native sandbox allows keyctl (if not: refuse native for granted seats, use posture=aida); Q2 whether codex sandbox applies shell_environment_policy like exec does; Q3 no registry token in the pointer; Q4 identity fallbacks in the same PR.

Pre-existing observation, to file separately: children already possess the parent's and siblings' grant keys through the linked or reused launcher keyring.
subject: BUG-2398 sketch posted (awaiting independent signoff)
